extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent examiners (U.S. patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for preparing, submitting, correcting, and accepting drawings and photographs in U.S. utility, design, and plant patent applications under 37 CFR 1.84 and MPEP §608.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation and sheet turning for wide views
rubrics_metrics.description: If views wider than the width of the sheet are necessary for the clearest illustration of the invention, the sheet may be turned on its side so that the top of the sheet ... is on the right-hand side. Words must appear in a horizontal, left-to-right fashion when the page is either upright or turned so that the top becomes the right side, except for graphs utilizing standard scientific convention to denote the axis of abscissas (of X) and the axis of ordinates (of Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets may be turned to accommodate wide views; text must remain horizontal left-to-right in either upright or turned orientation; graphs may follow standard axis conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention. One of the views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines. Applicant may suggest a single view (by figure number) for inclusion on the front page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale to which a drawing is made must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when the drawing is reduced in size to two-thirds in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications such as “actual size” or “scale 1/2” on the drawings are not permitted since these lose their meaning with reproduction in a different format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process which will give them satisfactory reproduction characteristics. Every line, number, and letter must be durable, clean, black (except for color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, and uniformly thick and well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight of lines and letters must permit adequate reproduction; requirement applies to fine lines, shading, and cut-surface lines. Different line thicknesses may be used where they have different meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of shading in views is encouraged if it aids in understanding the invention and if it does not reduce legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shading indicates surface/shape of spherical, cylindrical, conical elements; flat parts may be lightly shaded; spaced thin lines preferred; heavy lines on shade side acceptable as substitute except where they obscure reference characters; light should come from upper left at 45°. Solid black shading areas are not permitted, except for bar graphs or color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements represented by symbols must be adequately identified in the specification. Known devices should use symbols with universally recognized meaning. Other symbols may be used subject to Office approval if not likely to be confused and readily identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used subject to approval by the Office, or may be required by the examiner where necessary for understanding of the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legends should contain as few words as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters and orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals are preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain and legible, and must not be used in association with brackets or inverted commas, or enclosed within outlines, e.g., encircled. They must be oriented in the same direction as the view so as to avoid having to rotate the sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters should be arranged to follow the profile of the object depicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabet and character sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: The English alphabet must be used for letters, except where another alphabet is customarily used, such as the Greek alphabet to indicate angles, wavelengths, and mathematical formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers, letters, and reference characters must measure at least .32 cm (1/8 inch) in height and should not interfere with comprehension; they should not cross or mingle with lines or be placed on hatched/shaded surfaces. If placed on hatching for necessary indication, the character may be underlined and a blank left in the hatching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of reference characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The same part of an invention appearing in more than one view of the drawing must always be designated by the same reference character, and the same reference character must never be used to designate different parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters mentioned in the description must appear in the drawings; characters not mentioned shall not appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines are those lines between the reference characters and the details referred to. Such lines may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines must originate in the immediate proximity of the reference character and extend to the feature indicated; must not cross each other; required for each reference character except those which indicate the surface or cross section on which they are placed (such reference characters must be underlined). Lead lines must be executed in the same way as lines in the drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at the ends of lines, provided that their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible uses include: (1) freestanding arrow on a lead line to indicate entire section towards which it points; (2) arrow touching a line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along the direction of the arrow; (3) to show direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice placement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing, but must be placed within the sight of the drawing immediately below the figure representing the copyright or mask work material and be limited to letters having a print size of .32 cm. to .64 cm. (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high. The content of the notice must be limited to only those elements provided for by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion permitted only if the authorization language set forth in § 1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals, starting with 1, within the sight as defined in paragraph (g) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (but not in the margin), or on the right-hand side if drawing extends too close to middle; numbering must be clear and larger than reference characters; show sheet number and total number as two Arabic numerals separated by oblique line (e.g., '1/3').

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views
rubrics_metrics.description: The different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals, starting with 1, independent of the numbering of the sheets and, if possible, in the order in which they appear on the drawing sheet(s). Partial views intended to form one complete view must be identified by the same number followed by a capital letter. View numbers must be preceded by the abbreviation “FIG.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only a single view is used, it must not be numbered and 'FIG.' must not appear. View numbers and letters identifying views must be simple and clear and not enclosed; view numbers must be larger than reference character numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on the drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability of corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type and format consistency of drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are currently accepted in two different size formats. It is, however, required that all drawing sheets in a particular application be the same size for ease of handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Good quality copies are acceptable if the lines are uniformly thick, black, and solid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling replacement/new drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of an application must be identified as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' so that the Office will recognize how to treat such a drawing sheet for entry into the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections to drawings must be made in the form of replacement sheets labeled 'Replacement Sheet' since the Office does not release drawings for correction. If a marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure is filed, it must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet.' See 37 CFR 1.84(c) and 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are permitted to be transmitted by facsimile if the drawings are being submitted after the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure the facsimile transmission process does not unreasonably degrade the quality of the drawings. Color drawings are not permitted to be transmitted by facsimile. See 37 CFR 1.6(d)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of drawing categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: Original drawings (submitted with the application when filed); Substitute drawing (filed later than filing date, usually to replace unacceptable original); Acceptable drawing (acceptable for publication/issuance); Corrected drawing (includes corrections of informalities and examiner-approved changes); Unacceptable drawing (does not comply with form requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office no longer uses 'formal' or 'informal' classifications—drawings are either acceptable or unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black and white ink drawing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required in utility patent applications. India ink, or its equivalent that secures solid black lines, must be used for drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §608.02(c) for location of drawings in IFW applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black and white photographs / grayscale drawings — limited acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, including photocopies of photographs, are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications, but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (e.g., electrophoresis gels, blots, autoradiographs, cell cultures, histological tissue cross sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, thin layer chromatography plates, crystalline structures, metallurgical microstructures, textile fabrics, grain structures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject matter admits illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead. Photographs must be of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible in the printed patent. Black and white photographs submitted in lieu of ink drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84(b); no petition or fee required; only one set of photographs is required when via EFS-Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings and color photographs — design vs. utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings are permitted in design applications without a petition. Color drawings or color photographs are permitted in utility applications only on rare occasions and only after granting a petition under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2) explaining why color is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include fee (§1.17(h)), one set of color drawings if via EFS-Web (or three sets if paper), and an amendment to the specification inserting the specified language notifying that at least one drawing is in color. Color drawings must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in black and white in the printed patent. Color materials are not permitted in international applications (PCT Rule 11.13). Petition decided by a Supervisory Patent Examiner. Patent copies printed at issuance will depict drawings in black and white; color set will be attached to Letters Patent and copies with color provided on request for a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbol standards and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: ANSI and ISO publications include graphical symbols considered generally acceptable in patent drawings. Although these documents may be used as guides, the Office will not 'approve' any published collection of symbols as a group because use and clarity must be decided case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly specific symbols and symbols with unclear meanings. Label unclear symbols for clarification. In design patents, use graphic symbols judiciously because they may interfere with clear showing of the design; color drawings may be preferred for representing color rather than graphic symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of conventional material symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: The following symbols should be used to indicate various materials where the material is an important feature of the invention. The use of conventional features is very helpful in making prior art searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Note: the specific symbol list appears in following pages.)

rubrics_metrics.name: When new/ replacement drawings are required before examination
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP will review drawings in utility and plant applications for compliance with certain requirements of 37 CFR 1.84. OPAP will send a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers if the drawings are unacceptable for purposes of publication; the notice gives applicant two (2) months from mailing to file acceptable drawings (extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a)). OPAP will not release applications to Technology Centers until acceptable drawings are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at initial assignment or at time of action the supervisory patent examiner believes drawings do not permit reasonable examination, applicant should be required to immediately submit corrected drawings. If drawings permit reasonable examination but render application defective under 35 U.S.C. 112, examination should begin with requirement for corrected drawings and a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a). If OPAP indicated drawings as 'informal' but OPAP considers acceptable, examiner should not require replacement. Examiner objections should require correction in reply to Office action and not be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely filed drawings cause abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drawing is not timely received in reply to a notice from the Office or a letter from the examiner who requires a drawing, the application becomes abandoned for failure to reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability and placement for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility or plant application will not be placed on the files for examination until objections to the drawings have been corrected. Except as provided in § 1.215(c), any patent application publication will not include drawings filed after the application has been placed on the files for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction; new corrected drawings must be submitted within time set by the Office. If corrections are necessary after allowance, Office may set a non-extendable three-month period to file corrected drawings to avoid abandonment (37 CFR 1.85(c)). Objections to drawings will not be held in abeyance; drawing corrections should be made promptly before allowance to avoid delays or reductions to term adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties regarding drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should review the drawings for disclosure of the claimed invention and for proper use of reference numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are directed to advise applicants in the first Office action of the reasons why the drawings are unacceptable. If the examiner discovers a defect in the content of the drawing, form paragraphs may be used to notify applicant and require corrected drawings in reply to the Office action; objections will not be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and required content when notifying applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard form paragraphs (e.g., ¶6.21, ¶6.22, ¶6.26, ¶6.27) are used to notify applicants when new corrected drawings are required, when drawings are objected to, when drawings do not permit examination, and to require a marked-up copy of drawing corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ¶6.21 advises to employ a competent patent draftsperson; ¶6.22 explains that replacement drawing sheets must include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, figures to be canceled must be removed (remaining figures renumbered), replacement sheets must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet', and objections will not be held in abeyance. ¶6.26 may be used when drawings do not permit examination and gives applicant a shortened TWO MONTHS statutory period (extendable only as allowed) to submit replacements or risk abandonment. ¶6.27 requires submission of an 'Annotated Sheet' showing annotations of changes; failure to timely submit corrected drawing and marked-up copy will result in abandonment.
